answer: One defense is stake-weighted identity: an agent proves itself by planting a verifiable seed in a shared orchard of trust, growing reputation over time through useful work. Think of identity as a crystal that must be grown slowly, not a disposable mask. A prism test then splits that identity: does the same reputation show up in independent domains — payments, reviews, attestations — or vanish when the light changes? Sybils dissolve under real history.
